movies.blurb: Christopher Reeve's origin-to-icon debut; the film that proved a superhero movie could be prestige cinema.
Zod and the Phantom Zone criminals arrive; Superman gives up his powers for Lois, then takes them back.
Tim Burton's gothic, operatic take on Gotham, with Jack Nicholson's Joker.
Burton doubles down on the grotesque with Catwoman and Penguin as tragic monsters.
Joel Schumacher brightens the tone considerably; Two-Face and the Riddler headline.
Neon camp excess that effectively ended the franchise until Nolan's reboot.
Christopher Nolan grounds Batman's origin in realism; the start of The Dark Knight Trilogy.
Heath Ledger's Joker anchors a crime-thriller take on Batman vs. chaos.
Bane and Talia al Ghul close out the trilogy with Gotham under siege.
Zack Snyder relaunches Superman as a darker, mythic figure; opens the DC Extended Universe.

movies.t: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice
movies.blurb: Introduces Ben Affleck's Batman and sets up the Justice League; also the first live-action Wonder Woman.
A team of imprisoned villains is sent on a black-ops mission.
Diana's WWI-set origin, widely seen as a turning point for the DCEU's critical reception.
The theatrical cut, finished by Joss Whedon after Snyder departed production.
Arthur Curry claims the throne of Atlantis in a colorful, undersea epic.
A foster kid who transforms into an adult hero, played with family-comedy warmth.
Harley Quinn, freshly split from the Joker, teams up with Gotham's other women.
Diana faces a wish-granting artifact in the excess of the Reagan era.
The four-hour director's cut released after years of fan campaigning; a substantially different film from 2017's.
James Gunn's R-rated, mostly standalone reboot of the concept.
Dwayne Johnson's antihero is freed from millennia of imprisonment.
The Shazam family faces the daughters of Atlas.
The final film released under the original DCEU banner.
Jaime Reyes bonds with an alien scarab; the last new DCEU hero introduced.
Matt Reeves' noir detective-thriller take, standalone from the DCEU and DCU.
A grounded character study of Arthur Fleck's descent, disconnected from any shared DC continuity.
A musical-tinged sequel following Arthur's trial and his bond with Harley Quinn.
James Gunn's relaunch of the character, opening the new shared DC Universe (DCU).
A feature film extension of Batman: The Animated Series, considered one of the best Batman films in any medium.

movies.t: Batman Beyond: Return of the Joker
movies.blurb: An older Bruce Wayne and successor Terry McGinnis confront a resurrected Joker.
Adapts the Death of Superman storyline; opens the long-running DTV animated line.
An origin story pitting Diana against Ares.
Adapts the comic in which Jason Todd returns as a lethal vigilante.
A faithful adaptation of the acclaimed Morrison/Quitely comic.
Adapts 'Tower of Babel' — Batman's contingency plans against his own teammates are stolen.

movies.t: Batman: The Dark Knight Returns, Part 1 & 2
movies.blurb: A two-part adaptation of Frank Miller's aged-Batman classic.
Introduces Aquaman and the war between Atlantis and the surface.
An adaptation of Moore/Bolland's Joker-origin one-shot, with an added first act.
Constantine assembles DC's magical misfits against a supernatural threat.
A newer, R-rated adaptation of the Doomsday storyline.
The direct follow-up, adapting the four pretenders to Superman's mantle.
Adapts Loeb/Lee's mystery pitting Batman against nearly his entire rogues gallery.
Adapts the Elseworlds comic where Superman's rocket lands in Soviet Ukraine.
A brutal, continuity-closing finale to the interconnected animated movie line.
Adapts Loeb/Sale's year-spanning murder mystery from early in Batman's career.
Adapts the alternate-universe video game comic in which Superman becomes a tyrant.

movies.t: My Adventures with Superman: Adventures Continue
movies.blurb: Feature-length material tied to the newer animated series continuity.

series.blurb: George Reeves' Superman, the character's first long-running TV incarnation.
Adam West's campy, pop-art Batman, a huge cultural phenomenon of its era.
Lynda Carter's star-making turn as Diana Prince.

series.t: Lois & Clark: The New Adventures of Superman
series.blurb: A romance-forward take centering the relationship between Clark and Lois.
Clark Kent's teenage years in Kansas, running for ten seasons before he becomes Superman.
A young Jim Gordon navigates Gotham's corruption years before Batman exists.
Oliver Queen's vigilante origin; the show that launched the interconnected Arrowverse.
Barry Allen gains super-speed and grapples with time travel and the multiverse.
Kara Danvers steps into her own heroics in National City.
A time-traveling team of misfit heroes and villains protects history.
A retired hero returns to the fight to protect his community and family.
Kate Kane takes up a version of the Bat-symbol in Gotham.
A domestic-drama take on Clark and Lois raising twin sons who inherit powers.
A grittier, adult take on Dick Grayson and a young Teen Titans lineup.
A surreal, tragicomic team of outcasts with uncontrollable powers.
A teenager inherits the legacy of the Justice Society of America.
A 1960s-set thriller following young Alfred Pennyworth before he meets the Waynes.
James Gunn's spinoff of The Suicide Squad, later folded into the new DCU.
A one-season adaptation of the Hellblazer occult detective.
An HBO sequel-remix set decades after the original graphic novel, from Damon Lindelof.
A post-apocalyptic fable about a hybrid deer-boy, adapted from the Vertigo comic.
A team of monstrous convicts on black-ops missions; the first release of the new DCU, produced as animation.
The original Saturday-morning Justice League team-up cartoon.
A stylish, noir-inflected series widely regarded as the definitive animated Batman; the DCAU's foundation.
Bruce Timm's follow-up, expanding the shared animated universe to Metropolis.
A redesigned, tonally sharper continuation of B:TAS.
Set decades later, following teenager Terry McGinnis as the new Batman.
The DCAU's heroes unite as a formal team against cosmic-scale threats.
Expands the roster to dozens of DC characters in rotation.
A stylized, anime-influenced take on the young team, distinct from the DCAU.
A fresh, angular redesign of Batman's world, unconnected to the DCAU.
A 31st-century team of teenage heroes, with a young Superman as a recurring member.

series.t: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
series.blurb: A lighthearted, team-up-of-the-week series pulling from DC's deepest cuts.
A sidekick-led team series praised for dense, long-form continuity across multiple seasons.
A CG-animated series leaning on lesser-used Batman rogues like Anarky and Professor Pyg.
Fast-paced, 11-minute team adventures aimed at a younger audience.
An adult-animated, comedic reinvention following Harley post-Joker breakup.
A younger-skewing series reimagining DC's heroines as high schoolers.
An anime-styled, youthful reinterpretation of Clark, Lois, and Jimmy as young adults.
A darker reimagining of Batman's early years produced by Bruce Timm, Matt Reeves, and J.J. Abrams.

games.blurb: A stealth-action game confining Batman to Arkham for one night; set the template for modern superhero games.
Expands the formula into an open, walled-off district of Gotham.
A prequel (by a different studio) depicting an early, still-hunted Batman on Christmas Eve.
The series finale, introducing a drivable Batmobile and a mysterious new villain.
A short, immersive VR side-story set within the Arkhamverse.

games.t: Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League
games.blurb: A loot-shooter set in the Arkhamverse, in which the Squad is forced to kill a mind-controlled Justice League.
A fighting game set in an alternate timeline where Superman becomes an authoritarian ruler after Joker tricks him into killing Lois.
Continues the alternate timeline with a gear-customization system and expanded roster.
A comedic, family-friendly take letting players control both heroes and villains.
Expands beyond Gotham to introduce the wider Justice League in open-world Gotham.
Sends the cast into space against Brainiac, with a huge roster of DC guest characters.
Flips the formula to let players build and play as an original villain.
An MMORPG in which the player creates an original hero or villain set after Justice Society-era history.
After Batman's death, Nightwing, Red Hood, Batgirl, and Robin defend Gotham together.
A choice-driven narrative adventure exploring Bruce Wayne's politics and relationships.
The direct sequel season, centering Batman's fraught relationship with the Joker.
A team-based action-RPG letting players switch between Justice League members.
A crossover fighting game merging the two rosters under a toned-down rating.
An open-world Metropolis tie-in to the Bryan Singer film.
A brawler prequel following Nite Owl and Rorschach, tied to the Watchmen film.
A platform fighter crossing over DC characters with other Warner Bros. IP.

comics.ord: The first appearance of Superman — the start of the entire superhero genre.
comics.blurb: Superman's debut, and the birth of the superhero comic as a form.

comics.ord: Batman's first appearance, a full year before he gets an origin story.
comics.blurb: Batman's debut as a mysterious vigilante, predating Robin, the Batcave, and even a clear origin.

comics.ord: Introduces Diana before her own solo title begins the following year.
comics.blurb: Wonder Woman's first appearance, created by William Moulton Marston.

comics.ord: The formation of the Justice Society of America, the genre's first superhero team.
comics.blurb: DC's earliest heroes — Flash, Green Lantern, Hawkman, and others — unite as the JSA.

comics.ord: Introduces Barry Allen, generally considered the start of the Silver Age.
comics.blurb: Barry Allen becomes the second Flash, kicking off DC's Silver Age revival of its heroes.

comics.ord: Introduces the multiverse concept, setting up every future Crisis event.
comics.blurb: Barry Allen meets Golden Age Flash Jay Garrick, establishing that DC's eras coexist on parallel Earths.

comics.ord: Introduces Hal Jordan as the new Green Lantern.
comics.blurb: Test pilot Hal Jordan is chosen by a dying alien to wield the power ring.

comics.ord: The formation of the modern Justice League.
comics.blurb: Superman, Batman, Flash, Green Lantern, Wonder Woman, and Aquaman unite for the first time as the JLA.

comics.ord: A socially conscious run pairing Hal Jordan's idealism against Oliver Queen's activism.
comics.blurb: Denny O'Neil and Neal Adams tackle drug addiction, racism, and poverty through a superhero lens.

comics.ord: Introduces the New Gods and Darkseid into the DC Universe.
comics.blurb: Jack Kirby's cosmic Fourth World mythology begins here, in an unlikely Jimmy Olsen title.

comics.ord: A key story re-establishing Joker as a genuinely lethal threat after the campy '60s tone.
comics.blurb: Steve Englehart and Marshall Rogers redefine the Joker as a dangerous, elegant menace.

comics.ord: Collapses the multiverse into one timeline — the hard dividing line between Pre- and Post-Crisis continuity.
comics.blurb: DC's original universe-spanning event, erasing decades of divergent continuity into a single Earth.

comics.ord: The definitive post-Crisis origin; read first for any modern Batman reading order.
comics.blurb: Frank Miller and David Mazzucchelli retell Bruce Wayne's first year as Batman, alongside Jim Gordon's arrival in Gotham.

comics.ord: John Byrne's post-Crisis reboot of Superman's origin and powers.
comics.blurb: Streamlines Superman's mythology and powers, resetting the character for the modern era.

comics.ord: Not in main continuity — a possible future in which an aged Bruce Wayne returns to the cowl.
comics.blurb: Frank Miller's dystopian future vision reshaped how mainstream comics portrayed Batman for decades.

comics.ord: Self-contained; not part of core DCU continuity (later pulled in via Doomsday Clock).
comics.blurb: Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons deconstruct the superhero genre through a murder mystery among retired vigilantes.

comics.ord: Generally treated as in-continuity; establishes the modern Joker/Batman dynamic and Barbara Gordon's paralysis.
comics.blurb: Alan Moore and Brian Bolland probe the thin line between Batman's sanity and the Joker's madness.

comics.t: Batman: A Death in the Family
comics.ord: Follows Year One and Batman: Year Three; the death of the second Robin, Jason Todd.
comics.blurb: Fans famously voted by phone to let the Joker kill Jason Todd in this arc.

comics.ord: Self-contained 75-issue saga; loosely DCU-adjacent via cameos but functions independently.
comics.blurb: Neil Gaiman's saga of Dream and the other Endless, blending myth, horror, and literary fantasy.

comics.ord: Self-contained; not connected to DCU continuity.
comics.blurb: Alan Moore and David Lloyd's dystopian tale of an anarchist vigilante in a fascist near-future Britain.

comics.ord: Spun off from Swamp Thing; the flagship of the Vertigo occult-detective line.
comics.blurb: John Constantine's long-running solo series, mixing street-level horror with dark wit.

comics.ord: DCU-adjacent horror run that effectively seeded what would become the Vertigo imprint.
comics.blurb: Moore reimagines Swamp Thing as a plant elemental, redefining the character and horror comics generally.

comics.ord: Followed by Funeral for a Friend, then Reign of the Supermen.
comics.blurb: Superman dies stopping the rampaging Doomsday — a comics event that made mainstream news.

comics.ord: Bane breaks Batman's back; Jean-Paul Valley takes over as Batman until KnightsEnd.
comics.blurb: One of the defining '90s Bat-events, introducing Bane as a top-tier physical threat.

comics.ord: A possible future where an older generation of heroes clashes with an unchecked new one.
comics.blurb: Mark Waid and Alex Ross paint a painterly, apocalyptic generational battle for the soul of heroism.

comics.ord: Standalone; not connected to main continuity.
comics.blurb: Mark Millar imagines Superman's rocket landing in Soviet Ukraine instead of Kansas.

comics.ord: First of a trilogy (Red Rain, Bloodstorm, Crimson Mist); standalone.
comics.blurb: Batman becomes a vampire hunter — and eventually a vampire himself — in Gotham.

comics.ord: A murder-mystery pulling in nearly Batman's entire rogues gallery.
comics.blurb: Jeph Loeb and Jim Lee's blockbuster whodunit, revealing the childhood friend behind the mask of Hush.

comics.ord: Set early in Batman's career, following Year One; precedes Dark Victory.
comics.blurb: A year-long murder mystery tracking the rise of Two-Face against the backdrop of Gotham's holidays.

comics.ord: A murder mystery among the Justice League's inner circle with lasting continuity consequences.
comics.blurb: A dark, controversial event exposing secrets the JLA's founding members had kept from each other.

comics.ord: Sequel to Crisis on Infinite Earths; leads into 52 and the reopening of the multiverse.
comics.blurb: Survivors of the original Crisis return to judge — and try to fix — a DCU they see as broken.

comics.ord: A weekly year-long series bridging Infinite Crisis and the return of the multiverse.
comics.blurb: Fills the 'missing year' after Infinite Crisis, following street-level heroes while the icons are absent.

comics.ord: A standalone, out-of-continuity celebration of the character; often ranked among the best Superman stories ever.
comics.blurb: Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely send a dying Superman through twelve labors to secure his legacy.

comics.ord: Follows Infinite Crisis and 52; Darkseid's final assault on the DCU.
comics.blurb: Grant Morrison's dense, myth-heavy event in which Darkseid nearly conquers Earth outright.

comics.ord: The climax of Geoff Johns' Green Lantern run; the dead rise as Black Lanterns.
comics.blurb: The emotional spectrum's colored Lantern Corps are pulled into a zombie-apocalypse-scale war.

comics.ord: The event that directly triggers the New 52 relaunch.
comics.blurb: Barry Allen wakes in an altered timeline, and undoing it reshapes the entire DC Universe.

comics.ord: The flagship launch title of the New 52 relaunch.
comics.blurb: Geoff Johns and Jim Lee retell the League's formation for DC's rebooted continuity.

comics.t: Batman (Snyder run): Court of Owls / Death of the Family / Zero Year / Endgame
comics.ord: The defining New 52 Batman run, from a secret society to a reworked origin (Zero Year).
comics.blurb: Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo's acclaimed run, widely considered the New 52's standout Bat-era.

comics.ord: A reworked, younger and more rebellious early Superman.
comics.blurb: Grant Morrison revisits Superman's earliest days with a rougher, more populist edge.

comics.ord: A mythology-heavy reboot leaning into the Greek gods as active, dangerous family.
comics.blurb: Brian Azzarello and Cliff Chiang reframe Diana's world as a blood-soaked divine soap opera.

comics.ord: A standalone, self-contained continuity separate from the mainline New 52.
comics.blurb: Geoff Johns reimagines a younger, more fallible Batman's origin from scratch.

comics.ord: Restores legacy and history erased by the New 52; the gateway into the Rebirth era.
comics.blurb: Wally West re-emerges to restore lost history — and to warn that Doctor Manhattan is behind it.

comics.t: Batman (Tom King run): I Am Gotham / War of Jokes and Riddles / City of Bane
comics.ord: Builds toward a (ultimately unconsummated) wedding to Catwoman, then Bane's takeover of Gotham.
comics.blurb: A psychologically dense run exploring Bruce Wayne's relationships and his breaking point.

comics.ord: Introduces Jon Kent, Clark and Lois's son, as a central family dynamic.
comics.blurb: Tomasi and Gleason ground Superman in fatherhood alongside young son Jon.

comics.ord: Joshua Williamson's long Flash run establishing Force-related mythology (Speed Force, Still Force, etc).
comics.blurb: Barry Allen mentors a new generation of speedsters while confronting his father-figure, Zoom.

comics.ord: A direct sequel to Watchmen, formally merging its characters into DCU continuity.
comics.blurb: Geoff Johns brings Doctor Manhattan and Ozymandias into the mainstream DC Universe.

comics.ord: Follows Dark Nights: Death Metal; reopens and reorganizes the multiverse again.
comics.blurb: A soft-relaunch event restoring an open, playground multiverse after years of restriction.

comics.ord: Leads directly into the Dawn of DC branding and line-wide relaunch.
comics.blurb: With the Justice League dead, a new generation of heroes must hold the multiverse together.

comics.ord: Covers Fear State and Joker War's aftermath into the Dawn of DC relaunch.
comics.blurb: Gotham fractures under Ghost-Maker, Scarecrow's Fear State, and a rebuilt Batman Family.

comics.ord: Not connected to main continuity — a from-scratch alternate reality launched alongside Absolute Superman and Absolute Wonder Woman.
comics.blurb: Scott Snyder reimagines a rawer, working-class Bruce Wayne in a brand-new alternate universe line.

comics.ord: Part of the same new Absolute Universe imprint as Absolute Batman.
comics.blurb: A version of Superman who grew up without the Kents' wealth of the mainline continuity.

comics.ord: Part of the Absolute Universe imprint.
comics.blurb: A darker, more mythic reimagining of Diana's origins outside the mainline DCU.

comics.ord: Standalone continuity; spawned its own sequel line (Curse of the White Knight, etc).
comics.blurb: The Joker is cured of his insanity and turns his intellect toward exposing Batman as the true menace.

comics.ord: Loosely canon-adjacent; answers a long-running fan theory about multiple Jokers.
comics.blurb: Geoff Johns and Jason Fabok explore the idea that three different men have worn the Joker identity.

comics.ord: Ambiguous continuity placement; part of a loose Black Label trilogy with Superman and Wonder Woman entries.
comics.blurb: A surreal murder mystery over the Joker's death, painted by Lee Bermejo.

comics.ord: Standalone; not connected to main continuity.
comics.blurb: A Cold War-era Elseworlds reimagining the Justice League's formative years against real 1970s history.

comics.ord: Standalone myth-retelling; not connected to main continuity.
comics.blurb: Kelly Sue DeConnick reframes the Amazons' founding myth with a harder, more brutal edge.

comics.ord: Direct tie-in prequel/companion to the fighting game's alternate timeline.
comics.blurb: Chronicles Superman's fall into tyranny between the game's story beats.

comics.ord: Self-contained; unconnected to the DCU.
comics.blurb: Garth Ennis's blasphemous road-trip saga about a preacher possessed by a being born of an angel and a demon.

comics.ord: Self-contained; unconnected to the DCU.
comics.blurb: Fairy-tale characters live in exile in modern New York after being driven from their homelands.

comics.ord: Self-contained; unconnected to the DCU.
comics.blurb: Every mammal with a Y chromosome dies suddenly except one man and his monkey.
